features.construct: Configuration and ordered changes of explicitly marked grammatical person and address in the lyric document
features.operational_definition: Annotate each ordered textual segment for overt first-, second- and third-person pronouns, possessives, morphologically marked finite verbs, vocatives and direct-speech spans. Produce a segment-level person-presence vector and a song-level count of changes between adjacent vectors. Unexpressed subjects and narrator identity remain unassigned.
features.unit: Ordered textual segment nested within song; song-level aggregation
features.output_type: multilabel categorical vector plus non-negative transition count

known_sources: performer labels that do not establish narrative identity

calibration.design: Independent double annotation of a stratified sample spanning English and Spanish cases and all ordered positions; report nominal agreement for person-presence labels and absolute disagreement for transition counts before full extraction.

features.textual_relevance: Explicit grammatical-person evidence could support point-of-view continuity while preserving the boundary between observable markers and inferred narrator identity.
features.musical_relevance: May later condition continuity of address across lyric sections; it has no current melodic or success interpretation.
features.research_question_enabled: Candidate only: how are explicit person configurations distributed and changed across an ordered HookLab lyric corpus after its data artifact and segmentation unit are mapped?
features.outcome: Segment-level explicit-person vector and song-level transition profile; no popularity or producer-preference outcome
features.population: SOURCE_FRAME_ESTABLISHED: C001-C100 in canonical source revision 72; feature-level eligibility remains pending language metadata, calibration and measurement-error audit

provenance.candidate_basis: HookLab migration checkpoint candidate domain; not an observed HookLab corpus feature
literature: Lee and Yeung (2016), direct-speech annotation, https://aclanthology.org/L16-1168/

features.construct: Configuration of textually recoverable participant referents
features.operational_definition: Identify mentions of persons or person-like participant referents and cluster only textually supported coreferent mentions. Produce distinct referent count, mention count per referent and entry/exit positions. Generic, collective and unresolved mentions retain separate labels; a referent is not called a character unless the annotation evidence supports persistence across segments.
features.unit: Mention and coreference chain nested within song
features.output_type: referent inventory, chain lengths and ordered presence matrix

calibration.design: Independent mention and coreference annotation on a stratified subset followed by coreference agreement metrics and qualitative adjudication before song-level counts are released.

features.textual_relevance: Participant continuity is required before character, relationship or information-progression variables can be computed without conflating pronouns and entities.
features.musical_relevance: May later support character continuity across approved sections; it does not imply a performer's vocal identity.
features.research_question_enabled: How many textually recoverable participant referents appear, recur and change across each eligible lyric document?
features.outcome: Referent inventory and ordered presence configuration; no psychological or success outcome
features.population: SOURCE_FRAME_ESTABLISHED: C001-C100 in canonical source revision 72; referent eligibility remains pending language metadata and calibration

provenance.candidate_basis: HookLab migration checkpoint candidate domain; not an observed HookLab corpus feature

features.construct: Directed configuration of explicitly stated relations and interactions between textually resolved participant referents
features.operational_definition: For each resolved referent pair, annotate only explicit kinship, affiliation, address or interaction predicates and their direction. Produce a typed edge list and ordered edge-presence matrix. Positive, negative, intimate or coercive valence is not assigned unless a separate validated codebook defines and anchors the label.
features.unit: Explicit relation or interaction statement nested within referent pair and song

calibration.design: Calibrate only after the participant-referent feature passes and a HookLab relation/interaction codebook is defined with inclusion, exclusion and boundary examples.

features.textual_relevance: A relationship graph requires stable referent resolution plus an explicit relation/interaction codebook; neither output is currently present as HookLab corpus data.
features.musical_relevance: May later support continuity of relational state across sections; it cannot prescribe lyric content or relationship valence.
features.research_question_enabled: What explicit participant relations and interactions are represented, and how do their configurations change across the ordered lyric document?
features.outcome: Typed explicit-edge configuration; no inferred relationship quality or audience response
features.population: SOURCE_FRAME_ESTABLISHED: C001-C100 in canonical source revision 72; relation codebook and feature eligibility remain pending
forbidden_interpretations: gender or sexuality without explicit evidence
stable social tie from a single interaction

provenance.candidate_basis: HookLab migration checkpoint candidate domain; not an observed HookLab corpus feature

features.construct: Textually represented opposition, obstruction or incompatible goals among resolved participants or states
features.unit: Pending: event, clause or coded observation

calibration.design: Requires a HookLab operational decision separating observable opposition from inferred conflict before calibration can be designed.

features.textual_relevance: Conflict is present in the Story Brief schema, but the current observational corpus has not yet yielded a complete, calibrated conflict representation codebook.
features.musical_relevance: Potential future Story Brief input only after definition, calibration, registered analysis and statistical promotion.
features.research_question_enabled: Pending construct closure: how is explicit opposition represented across eligible lyric documents?
forbidden_interpretations: violence or coercion without textual evidence

provenance.candidate_basis: HookLab migration checkpoint candidate domain; construct remains unoperationalized
literature: Alberhasky and Durkee (2024) provide a methodological precedent for lexical cognitive tension but do not validate a HookLab conflict construct, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0303188

features.construct: Explicit temporal expressions, event anchors and textually licensed temporal relations
features.operational_definition: Annotate explicit temporal expressions and event predicates, then record only textually licensed BEFORE, AFTER, SIMULTANEOUS, INCLUDES or UNRESOLVED relations. Produce counts by relation type and an ordered temporal-state profile. Real-world chronology is not reconstructed when the document underspecifies it.
features.unit: Temporal expression or event relation nested within ordered segment and song

calibration.design: Adapt a bounded TimeML subset to English and Spanish lyrics, double annotate a stratified sample and retain UNRESOLVED rather than forcing temporal order.

features.textual_relevance: Explicit temporal anchors and relations could support temporal continuity, subject to a lyric-domain operationalization and calibration.
features.musical_relevance: May later support temporal continuity between approved sections; it does not infer musical time or beat position.
features.research_question_enabled: Which explicit temporal anchors and relations occur, and how does the textual temporal state change across eligible lyric documents?
features.outcome: Temporal graph and ordered relation profile; no real-world factual chronology
features.population: SOURCE_FRAME_ESTABLISHED: C001-C100 in canonical source revision 72; temporal annotation eligibility remains pending language metadata and calibration

provenance.candidate_basis: HookLab migration checkpoint candidate domain; not an observed HookLab corpus feature

features.construct: Ordered trajectory of affective states explicitly attributed in the lyric text
features.operational_definition: Annotate spans that explicitly name or predicate an affective state, its textual experiencer when resolvable, and its ordered position. Map labels to a documented valence-arousal representation only after bilingual human validation. Preserve ABSENT, AMBIGUOUS and UNRESOLVED states; exclude emotions merely evoked in listeners.
features.unit: Explicit affect-state span nested within ordered segment, experiencer and song
features.output_type: ordered explicit-state sequence with optional calibrated valence-arousal values

calibration.design: Construct a bilingual annotation guide, independently annotate explicit affect spans and compare human labels before evaluating any lexicon or model. Automatic provider/version must be frozen and validated separately if introduced.

features.textual_relevance: The Story Brief contains an emotional-trajectory field, but a statistical feature must separately measure explicitly represented textual affect and exclude listener effects.
features.musical_relevance: May later support continuity of represented affect across lyric sections; it cannot stand for music-evoked emotion.
features.research_question_enabled: What explicitly represented affective states occur, to whom are they attributed, and how do they change in textual order?
features.outcome: Ordered explicit affect-state profile; evoked listener emotion excluded
features.population: SOURCE_FRAME_ESTABLISHED: C001-C100 in canonical source revision 72; affect annotation provider and feature eligibility remain pending

provenance.candidate_basis: HookLab migration checkpoint candidate domain; not an observed HookLab corpus feature
literature: Mohammad (2022), ethics of automatic emotion recognition, https://aclanthology.org/2022.cl-2.1/

features.construct: Structural metadata describing the intended or documented function of a song section
features.operational_definition: Retain normalized section labels only as metadata. POD-LC observation lines are not converted into verse, chorus or bridge labels. Section labels never become lyric tokens and are not reanalyzed as a formal-architecture predictor without NEW_EVIDENCE=true and a new ANALYSIS_ID.

calibration.design: No new formal-section measurement is authorized in this registry version.

features.textual_relevance: The metadata boundary prevents section names from contaminating lyric content and preserves STORY_BRIEF != SECTION_FUNCTION != LYRIC_CONTENT.
features.musical_relevance: Section function can condition creative role after producer selection; it is not an empirical success rule.
features.research_question_enabled: None in this registry version; formal architecture family frozen
features.population: HookLab generated sections; corpus-wide formal inference not reopened
forbidden_interpretations: POD-LC line as formal song section

features.construct: Ordered introduction, recurrence and closure of textually identifiable referents, events, locations and states
features.operational_definition: For each ordered segment, classify validated referent, event, location and state mentions as NEW, GIVEN, BRIDGING or UNRESOLVED relative to prior text; compute type-specific novelty proportions and change between adjacent segments. Repeated chorus material remains in the denominator and is also reported in a sensitivity analysis with repeated blocks collapsed.
features.unit: Validated mention nested within ordered segment and song
features.output_type: type-specific information-status sequence and novelty proportions

calibration.design: Adapt NEW/GIVEN/BRIDGING annotation after referent and event units are calibrated. Compare documentary segments with a predeclared sensitivity segmentation; do not select the segmentation from the observed direction.

features.textual_relevance: The construct directly addresses whether later sections add information or repeat established material while respecting documentary order.
features.musical_relevance: May later help the AI coherence layer detect semantic redundancy and advancement of open threads; it cannot define quality or prescribe a section's content.
features.research_question_enabled: How do new, given, bridging and unresolved information units change across the ordered lyric document?
features.outcome: Type-specific novelty and recurrence profile; no popularity, quality or causal outcome
features.population: SOURCE_FRAME_ESTABLISHED: C001-C100 in canonical source revision 72; referent/event units and feature eligibility remain pending

provenance.candidate_basis: HookLab migration checkpoint candidate domain; not an observed HookLab corpus feature
literature: Alberhasky and Durkee (2024), lyric narrative segmentation limitations, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0303188
